transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I've been having some issues with my eating habits lately. What really made me decide to come in is that... well, after some long days on the construction site, or sometimes after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll come home and just eat way more than I ever meant to. 

I end up going through whatever’s there—leftover takeout, cereal, chips, really anything I can find. And I just keep eating until I’m uncomfortably full. It's been bothering me, so I figured I should finally talk to someone about it.
When you're eating this way, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start on those evenings, it... it really just feels like I’m on autopilot. I’ll actually be telling myself to stop, knowing I have an early crew start the next morning, but I just keep going back to the kitchen for more anyway. I just can't seem to cut myself off once it happens.
Does this pattern of eating cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah, it definitely causes me some distress. I mean, I’m still showing up and doing my job just fine, so work is okay. But... it is starting to affect things outside of that. I’ve actually started turning down some after-meeting food plans, or I just find myself rushing straight home. I guess I'm just worried that the evening will get away from me if I'm not careful. So, it is definitely getting in the way a bit.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate for the food you’ve eaten?

Yeah, I do. I don't use laxatives or go crazy at the gym, but... a few times a month, after one of those really bad nights, I have gone into the bathroom and made myself throw up. I just... I get this sudden panic right after I eat all that. I worry about undoing all the work I’ve put into looking put-together, so... yeah, I do make myself sick.
How often do you find yourself making yourself vomit after these episodes of overeating, and does it happen every time you overeat or only occasionally?

It doesn't happen every single time I overeat, no. But... if I look back over the last few months, the whole pattern—the overeating and then making myself sick—it averages out to about once a week. Some weeks it might happen twice, and then other weeks I might not do it at all. But yeah, on average, it's about weekly.

When you have these episodes where you overeat and then make yourself vomit, do they feel like distinct events that happen together, and do you feel that your eating during these episodes is definitely out of your control?

Yeah, they definitely happen together. The throwing up is always right after I eat like that. And as for the eating... yeah, it really does feel out of my control. Once I start on those evenings, it feels like I’m just on autopilot. I'll be in my head, telling myself to stop because I have an early crew start the next morning and I need to be sharp, but... I just keep going back to the kitchen for more anyway. I can't seem to stop myself once it starts.
When you find yourself overeating and then making yourself vomit, is that mainly because you're feeling upset or worried about your body weight or shape?

Yeah, it really is. Lately... well, since I started wearing more fitted work clothes and being up front at meetings more often, my shape has been on my mind a lot. I actually catch myself judging my whole day just by whether my pants feel tight in the morning, or whether I think people can see my stomach. So, yeah, worrying about how I look is definitely what drives it.
Do these episodes of overeating and making yourself vomit tend to happen when you're feeling down, stressed, or alone, or do they seem to come on regardless of how you're feeling emotionally?

I'm not entirely sure, honestly. I haven't really tracked if it's tied to a specific mood. Sometimes I guess I might be stressed from work, but other times it just happens. I haven't noticed a clear pattern with how I'm feeling emotionally when it starts.
